docs.title: Dough (~10 thin rounds)
docs.text:
• Warm water: 1 cup (240 g)
  • Instant yeast: 1.5 tsp (5 g)
  • Sugar: 1 tsp (4 g)
  • Bread: 3 cups (360 g)
  • Salt: 1.5 tsp (9 g)
  • Olive oil: 1 tbsp (15 g)

docs.title: Meat Topping
docs.text:
• Ground beef: 1.5 lb (~1 costco pack)
  • Onion: 1 medium (~150 g)
  • Garlic: 3 cloves (~12 g)
  • Red bell pepper: 1 small (~120 g)
  • Flat-leaf parsley: 1 cup packed (~40 g)
  • Tomato paste: 3 tbsp (50 g)
  • Olive oil: 2 tbsp (30 g)
  • Paprika: 2 tsp (4 g)
  • Aleppo pepper: 2 tsp (4 g)
  • Cumin: 1 tsp (2 g)
  • Salt: 15 g
  • Black pepper: 1 tsp (2 g)

docs.title: 1. Make the Dough
docs.text:
1. Mix warm water, yeast, sugar. Rest 5 min.
  2. Add flour, salt, olive oil. Knead 8–10 min until smooth.
  3. Cover and rise 1 hour until doubled.
  4. Divide into 60 g balls (~10); rest 15 min.

docs.title: 2. Make the Topping
docs.text:
1. In the processor: onion chunks, garlic, bell pepper → pulse to a fine mince, not a puree.
  2. Add parsley → quick pulses to incorporate.
  3. Move veg mix to a bowl.
  4. Add ground beef, tomato paste, olive oil, paprika, Aleppo, cumin, salt, pepper.
  5. Mix thoroughly.

docs.title: 3. Shape the Bases
docs.text:
1. Preheat oven to 475°F. Place your sheet pan inside to preheat.
  2. Roll each dough ball very thin. You want almost tortilla-thin.

docs.title: 4. Assemble
docs.text:
1. Lay parchment on another sheet pan (not in the oven) and brush some oil on.
  2. Place rolled dough rounds on parchment. Spread a thin, even layer of topping, edge-to-edge.

docs.title: 5. Bake
docs.text:
1. Keep Sheet Pan A in the oven so it stays hot.
  2. Build each lahmacun on parchment on Sheet Pan B (counter).
  3. Slide parchment from B onto hot Pan A and bake ~8 minutes.
  4. While it bakes, assemble the next one on B.
  5. When A comes out, slide off the cooked one, slide the new parchment from B onto A, and return A to the oven.
  6. Repeat — A always stays hot in the oven; B is only for assembly.

docs.title: 6. Serve
docs.text:
• Squeeze lemon.
  • Add onion–parsley–sumac salad.
  • Roll and eat immediately.

docs.title: Gravy
docs.text:
• Unsalted butter: 3 Tbsp
  • All-purpose flour: 3 Tbsp
  • Beef stock: 2 cups
  • Soy sauce: 1 Tbsp
  • Worcestershire sauce: 1 tsp
  • Onion powder: ½ tsp
  • Garlic powder: ½ tsp
  • Black pepper: to taste

docs.title: 1. Cook the Rice
docs.text: 1. Start rice in the cooker so it finishes with everything else.

docs.title: 2. Make the Gravy
docs.text:
1. Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat.
  2. Whisk in flour; cook 2–3 min until lightly golden and nutty.
  3. Slowly whisk in beef stock until smooth.
  4. Add soy, Worcestershire, onion powder, garlic powder, black pepper.
  5. Simmer until thick and glossy; adjust seasoning.

docs.title: 5. Assemble
docs.text:
1. In each bowl: rice → burger → ladle of gravy → fried egg.
  2. Garnish with scallions and furikake or togarashi.
